l1.text: Ever wonder why you can feel okay right after a concussion… and then feel terrible later?

l2.text: That's because a concussion doesn't always cause something you can see from the outside.

l3.text: After an injury, the brain can temporarily have trouble communicating efficiently and managing the energy it needs to function normally.

l4.text: That can affect everything from concentration and memory to balance, energy, and how you process information.

l5.text: And symptoms can fluctuate. You might feel pretty good one day and struggle the next.

l6.text: Sometimes, too much physical or mental activity can temporarily make symptoms worse. That doesn't necessarily mean you're getting new brain damage—it can mean your brain needs a little more time and the right recovery strategy.

l7.text: If your symptoms are sticking around, don't just push through them. Get evaluated and find out what your brain needs.
